$comment: THE 📐 SPEC-DEBT BASELINE — 14 §6's build-time check.
14 §6 🔒: 'a build-time check enumerates every 📐 marker in the documentation set against
the schema keys and fails on a mismatch. That check is what stops the tuning surface eroding
over eighteen months.'
An exact 1:1 match is not reachable today and pretending otherwise would mean weakening the
check. This file is the honest alternative: every mismatch that exists right now, each with a
reason and — where one exists — the milestone task that closes it. The check FAILS on anything
not recorded here, and equally on an entry here that no longer describes a real mismatch — so
the file can only shrink without somebody arguing for it in a diff. It is a measurement of spec
debt, not a place to hide it.
Two directions:
unmatchedMarkers        — a 📐 marker in game-design/ whose doc section no schema key cites.
unmarkedSchemaCitations — a NUMERIC key in a tuning/ schema whose cited doc section carries
no 📐 marker. The tuning surface eroding from the other side.
🔒 TWO KINDS, and they are not the same thing:
"kind": "specDebt"    — a real hole that a real milestone task closes. MUST carry closedBy,
and that id must exist in IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md (a test asserts
it, reading the tracker). 'M0-11' used to sit on seven of these: a
task that has never existed, in a milestone that is complete.
"kind": "outOfScope"  — the marker is not a tunable at all: a glossary row, prose about the
rule itself, a verification instruction, an art-budget line, server
configuration. Nothing closes it because there is nothing to close, so
it carries NO closedBy. Conflating the two is how 'never' became a
synonym for 'unowned'. There are SEVEN of them and each one should be
argued with.
⚠️ The audit reads game-design/*.md and game-data/schema/*.json. It never reads
content/. An entry whose number lives in content/ therefore closes when that content type's
SCHEMA is authored and its description cites the section — not when the data files land. The
closedBy names the task that does both, and the reason says so.
Regenerate the SHAPE with:  dotnet run --project tools/ContentValidator -- --write-baseline
It writes kind: "unreviewed" and no owner, which the reader REFUSES — so a regenerated file
that nobody hand-edited fails loudly instead of accepting the literal 'TODO' as a reason.

unmatchedMarkers.reason: The glossary row that defines the 📐 marker itself. It is documentation about the rule, not a number.

Launch content counts (90 perks, 8 chapters, ...). Content identity, authored as files under content/. Closes when the last content catalogue and its schema exist and cite 01 §6 — the audit reads schema/, never content/.
Run and animation durations. 02 §1-3 is M3-05's spec: the run state machine authors the stage-gate timings and the schema key that holds them.
Campfire heal percentage. Belongs to the campfire tile, authored with the shrine/campfire/curse tiles.
Board topology: nodes per stage, fork count, fork length. Board generation is M3-01 (spec 03 §1-3); the keys land in the chapter content schema, not in tuning/.
The Portal jump range 3-6. 03 §1.1 is M3-02's spec — the movement engine authors the portal draw.
Chapter signature mechanics (Burning tile share, Clockwork pressure). 03 §4 is M3-12's spec; the keys land in chapter.schema.json alongside the content.
Minigame reward tables per chapter. currencies.json holds minigameRewards but the per-chapter split is unauthored; 03 §6 is M3-10's spec.
Dice reroll charges per stage. Doc 04 is M3-04's spec, which authors the reroll-charge economy. (Was M1-05, which is the Run aggregate and authors no dice weights.)
The die-face weighting constants (0.55 / 0.12 / clamps). Same owner as §3: M3-04's Fair-Dice weighted bag.
Dice animation timings and Fast Mode. Presentation: 04 §6 is named in M7-05's spec (Board S05 + Die Panel S12).
Chapter enemy-pool weights. Authored per chapter under content/chapters/; M3-14 authors the 8 chapter data files and the pool/weight keys.
Codex mastery bonuses (+17.2% all stats). 06 §6 is M4-11's spec (Codex model: per-entry stat bonuses, TP milestones).
Pet ability values. beasts.json holds the level/egg economy; the per-pet abilities are content/pets/, authored by M4-07 (spec 07 §2).
Mount stat blocks and run perks. content/mounts/, authored by M4-08 (spec 07 §3).
The free talent-preset allowance. A UX allowance the doc says to raise on telemetry, not an economy dial the simulator sweeps. Doc 09 is M4-06's spec, which authors the preset rules.
A verification instruction ('verify with the balance harness'), not a number that lives in a file.
The paragraph describing the simulator's role. Prose about 📐 numbers, not a 📐 number.
The PvP loadout Perk Point budget. PvP tuning has no file in the 21 §3.1 catalogue; 11 §3 is M12-02's spec, which authors the perk budget system and decides where the key lives.
PvP attempt refresh time. The attempt system (5/day + ad + Plus) is M12-06.
Matchmaking rating band and widening. 11 §4's matchmaking, incl. band widening, is M12-03.
JWT access and refresh lifetimes. Server configuration, not game content: it never reaches a ContentSnapshot and no schema will ever hold it.

A decision-log row quoting in-run economy numbers that currencies.json already owns. Closes when M4-09 wires the wallet/shop model and the currencies.json key cites 16, or when the duplicated numbers are struck from the log row. (Was M0-11, a task that has never existed.)

Part D's FTUE script (the tutorial-only heal, the fixed shop row). ftue.json is a sequencing file, not economy — and 19 numbers its sections 'PART D / D4.2', which the doc-section join cannot bind to at all. M4-12 authors ftue.json, its structural validator and its schema.
The sentence stating this very rule. Prose about the check, not a number.

The standard-chest pity ladder. luck.json holds hardPity and softPity, but the schema key cites 24 §4.2 rather than §4.1, so the join misses by one section. M4-02 owns 24 §4 (chest ladders, soft-pity slopes) and corrects the citation with the code that reads it. (Was M0-11, a task that has never existed.)
An instruction that counter strings are localisation keys and must be width-tested in German. Not a number.
An art-budget line (three dungeon-select illustrations). Not a tunable at all; it sits in the asset manifest.

The account-link one-time grant (500 Soul Shards + a chest). Belongs in currencies.json's earn sources; 28 has no numbered sections for the join. M16-01 authors account linking and its link reward. (Was M11-03, which is biome art batches.)

unmarkedSchemaCitations.reason: forge.json crownCostByOutputRarity cites 08 §4.1, whose 📐 marker sits in §4 (the Forge header) — the join is one level off, not absent. M4-04 implements 08 §4 and either moves the marker down or the citation up. (Was M0-11, a task that has never existed.)
forge.json stoneCostPerLevel cites 08 §4.2. 08 §4's 📐 marker covers it; the section granularity differs. Same owner as §4.1. (Was M0-11.)
beasts.json eggOdds cites 24 §4.4 (egg pity). 24's 📐 markers sit in §4.1 and §9; §4.4 itself carries none. M4-02 implements 24 §4 incl. egg P1-P3. (Was M0-11.)

forge.json stoneCostPerLevel carries 25 §7's E9 instruction to re-derive the +11..+15 costs by simulation. M18-03's joint economy tuning is the task that names exactly that re-derivation. (Was M8-01, which is art-licence confirmations.)

progression.json unlocks cites 26 §5 for the EVENTS gate. 26 carries one 📐 marker and it is elsewhere. 26 §5 is M13-06's spec (the EVT_EMBERFALL launch package). (Was M11-01, which is asset-manifest reconciliation.)

par_power.json tooWeakWarningRatio cites 29 §4.2. 29's markers are in §2-3 and §6; §4.2 states the warning ratio without one. M6-04 covers 29 §4-6 and explicitly wires the chapter-select warning that reads this key. (Was M0-11, a task that has never existed.)
